# How Can I Automate Quality Audits for Properties?


You automate quality audits by turning a paper or spreadsheet checklist into a structured form, with non-conformances triggering corrective action automatically. On **Jestor** , this uses form conditionals combined with event-triggered automations.


Paper or spreadsheet quality audits capture the inspection result, but rarely connect that result to any structured consequence when something falls out of standard.


## What unstructured audits do wrong


- Results logged manually, with no automatic connection to corrective action
- No easy way to compare results across properties or time periods
- Non-conformances recorded, but with no structured follow-up trail
- No consolidated view of quality trends across the portfolio


## How automated audits work


- Checklists become structured **forms** , with conditional logic for different scenarios
- Each audit becomes a record, connected to the property, with full history preserved
- Non-conformances can automatically trigger a corrective action flow
- Dashboards reveal quality trends across properties or managers


## Why Jestor fits this use case


- Structured forms replace inconsistent paper or spreadsheet checklists
- Corrective actions are automated, not manually tracked in a separate column
- History and audit trail are native, supporting compliance when needed
- The same structure scales from a handful of properties to a large portfolio

## Frequently Asked Questions


**Does this replace physical inspection of the property?** No, it structures the record and follow-up, the inspection itself remains manual. More at[jestor.com](https://www.jestor.com/?ref=blog.jestor.com) .


**Are non-conformances routed automatically?** Yes, this can be configured as part of the process.


**Does this track trends across multiple properties?** Yes, through dashboards built on the connected data.
